reason: The scoped-search finding is a concrete introduced performance defect, not merely the intentional bounded substring scan. A substring search must examine the selected session's text, but the optional-scope OR causes traversal of unrelated cached sessions too. The shipping tool always supplies its current session, and cache limits allow 4096 sessions and 1 GiB. Separating scoped SQL removes avoidable cache-wide work without changing substring semantics, snapshot revision checks or the schema.
evidence: Independently extracted the exact SQL from native-helper/src/index.rs and reproduced its table definitions in an in-memory Python SQLite 3.45.3 database with 100 sessions and 100 documents each; no repository files or persistent database were modified.

For the same no-match query scoped to s050, current SQL returned no rows and EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN reported SCAN d USING INDEX sqlite_autoindex_documents_1; it executed 50358 VM instructions. Changing only the optional-scope OR to d.session=?1 returned the same result, reported SEARCH d USING INDEX sqlite_autoindex_documents_1 (session=?), and executed 652 VM instructions.
native-helper/Cargo.toml selects rusqlite bundled SQLite; Cargo.lock pins libsqlite3-sys 0.30.1. Its installed sqlite3/sqlite3.c defines SQLITE_VERSION 3.46.0 at line 462.

Inspected the exact bundled SQLite amalgamation's exprAnalyzeOrTerm at lines 160834-160869 and 160909-160967: usable OR access requires all disjuncts to be indexable for the same table, intersects their table masks, and requires equality terms for OR-to-IN conversion. The parameter-only ?1 IS NULL disjunct is not a document-column constraint. The multi-index OR loop at lines 166687-166689 requires that resulting indexable mask. This supports the same planner limitation in the shipped dependency.

desktop/native/tools-plugin.mjs passes exec.agent.session.id into SessionTextIndex.search, and desktop/native/session-text.mjs includes that session ID in the helper search request. The all-session path exists but is not the shipping tool's normal use.
verification_boundary: VM counts and plans were executed with system SQLite 3.45.3; bundled SQLite 3.46.0 was inspected at source level, not executed in a new harness. This is query-work evidence, not a production wall-clock benchmark. A targeted query-plan check on the bundled version is appropriate when implementing the fix.
